# Project Task List

This is an initial plan toward the [desired outcome](../../README.md#outcome),
not a committed schedule. Review and prioritize the items before assigning
owners or dates. Existing documentation and its timelines are proposals to
reconcile with that outcome.

## 1. Revisit the project and establish a path forward

- [ ] Review the vision, whitepaper, research notes, roadmap, and archived README.
- [ ] Reconcile the existing celestial naming and citizen science concepts with
      the goal of a playable space exploration game and creator-owned content.
- [ ] Define the target audience, player experience, creator experience, and
      what success looks like.
- [ ] Inventory existing assets and identify documentation that is outdated,
      contradictory, or missing.
- [ ] Identify available contributors, skills, funding, dependencies, and risks.
- [ ] Prioritize the work, assign owners, and establish realistic milestones
      and timelines based on available resources.
- [ ] Update the project documentation and roadmap to reflect agreed decisions.

## 2. Define the game and economy

- [ ] Design the core exploration, discovery, progression, and interaction loops.
- [ ] Define the first playable experience and its minimum scope.
- [ ] Decide what types of space, objects, and creator-made content can be owned.
- [ ] Design creation, publishing, discovery, trading, and creator rewards.
- [ ] Define the relationship between real astronomical data, procedural content,
      and player-created content, including data licensing and attribution.
- [ ] Clarify digital ownership, content rights, moderation, and the distinction
      between game assets and real-world celestial bodies.
- [ ] Evaluate economic sustainability, accessibility, and relevant legal and
      regulatory considerations before committing to a token model.

## 3. Design and validate the technology

- [ ] Evaluate game engines, platforms, multiplayer needs, and infrastructure.
- [ ] Decide what belongs on-chain versus off-chain, including costs, privacy,
      performance, interoperability, and long-term availability.
- [ ] Evaluate blockchain networks, wallets, asset standards, and storage options.
- [ ] Define asset identity, metadata, provenance, ownership, and transfer models.
- [ ] Prototype the core exploration experience and validate it with players.
- [ ] Prototype creation and ownership of a digital asset on a test network.
- [ ] Document architecture, threat model, development setup, and test strategy.

## 4. Build and test a minimum viable game

- [ ] Implement a small explorable space environment and core gameplay loop.
- [ ] Add player identity and wallet connection with clear transaction feedback.
- [ ] Implement creation, tokenization, viewing, and transfer of scoped game assets.
- [ ] Integrate chosen data and content sources with appropriate attribution.
- [ ] Add creator discovery and the agreed initial ownership or trading flows.
- [ ] Test gameplay, accessibility, security, performance, and asset lifecycle.
- [ ] Obtain independent smart contract security review before a production launch.
- [ ] Run a limited test, gather feedback, and prioritize fixes.

## 5. Launch and iterate

- [ ] Establish deployment, monitoring, incident response, and recovery processes.
- [ ] Publish player, creator, contributor, and operational documentation.
- [ ] Define community support, moderation, governance, and feedback processes.
- [ ] Set launch criteria and verify legal, security, and operational readiness.
- [ ] Launch the agreed initial experience and measure its outcomes.
- [ ] Reassess priorities, resources, and timelines using player and creator feedback.
